findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] app/models/optimized_image.rb:~148 — `downsize` is defined twice: the new 4-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the 5-arg one, so every existing caller passing `width, height` binds `height` into `opts`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` inside `optimize` raises `TypeError` (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer), breaking thumbnail generation site-wide; the edited 5-arg method is dead code.

[High/security] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63–69 — there is no server-side upper bound on file size before the downsize loop; the 10MB cap exists only in client JS (trivially bypassed), so any authenticated client can POST an arbitrarily large file with an image filename and the server will run up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions on it inside the request (CPU/memory/disk exhaustion DoS), whereas previously oversized files were rejected by size validation before any image processing.

[High/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 and :246 — hardcoding `10 * 1024` replaces the site-setting-driven limits (`max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb`): admins who configure any limit above 10MB get legitimate uploads blocked client-side, non-image types (attachments, never downsized) pass the client check only to be rejected server-side, and the 413 handler always reports a 10MB limit even when the server enforces a different one.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — downsizing is done in place (`tempfile.path` passed as both `from` and `to`); ImageMagick `convert` with identical input/output paths is unreliable (the output can truncate the source before it is fully read, especially for large/multi-frame files), so a partial failure destroys the only copy of the upload — every other call site writes to a separate output path.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (`false` when convert exits non-zero) is ignored; if ImageMagick is missing or fails (corrupt image, disk full), the loop re-runs the same failing command 5 times and then passes the still-oversized or corrupted tempfile to `Upload.create_for`, producing confusing downstream errors instead of failing fast.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64–68 — the fixed strategy (5 attempts of "80%") does not guarantee the file reaches `max_image_size_kb` (encoded bytes don't shrink proportionally to pixel count; e.g. a 10MB upload with a sub-1MB limit is still oversized after 5 passes), so the upload is rejected anyway even though the client told the user anything up to 10MB would be accepted and auto-reduced; also up to 5 sequential convert runs per oversized upload is expensive.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 (with `OptimizedImage.optimize`) — the animated-GIF branch is chosen via `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` here is a Tempfile path (e.g. `/tmp/RackMultipart...` or `discourse-upload-...`) that never ends in `.gif`, so animated GIFs above the limit are always processed with the static-image instructions (no coalesce/frame handling), which can produce broken animations, and the `allow_animation:` option is effectively a no-op on this path.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` hardcodes the download cap instead of using `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and this API path serves all upload types so it also ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`; API uploads by URL larger than 10MB now fail even when the site's settings permit them.

[Low/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `allow_animation` is sourced from `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`, a setting intended to control animated *thumbnails*; using it to decide whether the stored original upload keeps its animation conflates two distinct behaviors.

[Medium/test_gap] No specs are added or updated in this diff — nothing covers the new `downsize` dimensions-string signature, the controller downsizing loop (success, non-convergence, convert failure), or the changed client-side limit; existing `OptimizedImage` specs calling `downsize(from, to, w, h)` would have exposed the duplicate-definition breakage.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63–69 — there is no server-side upper bound on file size before the downsize loop; the 10MB cap exists only in client JS (trivially bypassed), so any authenticated client can POST an arbitrarily large file with an image filename and the server will run up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick conversions on it inside the request (CPU/memory/disk exhaustion DoS), whereas previously oversized files were rejected by size validation before any image processing.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `UploadsController#create_upload` runs a downsize loop **before** `Upload.create_for(...)` (which is where size validations would typically happen) whenever `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` and the filename is an image. For direct uploads (`tempfile = file.tempfile`) there is no server-side cap added in this diff prior to invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times, so an authenticated client could POST a very large “image” and force multiple synchronous conversions during the request. The only explicit 10MB limit shown is in client JS and the URL-download path (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`), not the general upload path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — downsizing is done in place (`tempfile.path` passed as both `from` and `to`); ImageMagick `convert` with identical input/output paths is unreliable (the output can truncate the source before it is fully read, especially for large/multi-frame files), so a partial failure destroys the only copy of the upload — every other call site writes to a separate output path.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` downsizes images by calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e., the same file path is used for both input (`from`) and output (`to`). `OptimizedImage` ultimately shells out via `convert_with(...)` to perform the operation, so this is an in-place rewrite of the only upload copy. That creates a real risk of truncation/corruption on partial failure because the source and destination are identical.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (`false` when convert exits non-zero) is ignored; if ImageMagick is missing or fails (corrupt image, disk full), the loop re-runs the same failing command 5 times and then passes the still-oversized or corrupted tempfile to `Upload.create_for`, producing confusing downstream errors instead of failing fast.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb a new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times while `tempfile.size` remains above the limit, but it never checks the return value. In optimized_image.rb, `downsize` -> `optimize` -> `convert_with` returns `false` when the convert command exits non-zero (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`). If conversion fails (missing ImageMagick/corrupt image/etc.), the loop will rerun the same failing command 5 times and then proceed to `Upload.create_for` with an unmodified (still oversized or bad) tempfile, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64–68 — the fixed strategy (5 attempts of "80%") does not guarantee the file reaches `max_image_size_kb` (encoded bytes don't shrink proportionally to pixel count; e.g. a 10MB upload with a sub-1MB limit is still oversized after 5 passes), so the upload is rejected anyway even though the client told the user anything up to 10MB would be accepted and auto-reduced; also up to 5 sequential convert runs per oversized upload is expensive.

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side loop in `uploads_controller.rb` (5 passes of `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%")`) is only a best-effort reduction and does not ensure `tempfile.size` will end up <= `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`; after the loop it still calls `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)`, so an image can remain oversized and be rejected. This is especially problematic because the client-side check in `utilities.js` was changed to always allow up to `10*1024` KB (10MB) and will present that as the limit, creating a real mismatch where the UI implies acceptance but the server can still reject if downsizing doesn't get under the site setting. The “up to 5 sequential convert runs” cost is also directly implied by the `while attempt > 0` loop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 (with `OptimizedImage.optimize`) — the animated-GIF branch is chosen via `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, but `from` here is a Tempfile path (e.g. `/tmp/RackMultipart...` or `discourse-upload-...`) that never ends in `.gif`, so animated GIFs above the limit are always processed with the static-image instructions (no coalesce/frame handling), which can produce broken animations, and the `allow_animation:` option is effectively a no-op on this path.

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. In `optimized_image.rb`, the animated branch is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Here `from` is the tempfile path, and in the download-URL path the tempfile is created with basename `"discourse-upload-#{type}"` (no `.gif` extension), so the regex will not match and animated GIFs will be processed with non-animated instructions even when `allow_animation:` is passed. That can break/strip animations and makes `allow_animation:` ineffective on this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` hardcodes the download cap instead of using `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, and this API path serves all upload types so it also ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`; API uploads by URL larger than 10MB now fail even when the site's settings permit them.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL-download path was changed from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`, which hardcodes the maximum downloaded size and no longer respects the site-configured limit in this branch. This can cause URL-based API uploads >10MB to fail even if site settings would otherwise allow larger downloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `allow_animation` is sourced from `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`, a setting intended to control animated *thumbnails*; using it to decide whether the stored original upload keeps its animation conflates two distinct behaviors.

adjudication.rationale: The diff newly uses `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` when downsizing an over-limit image upload (`OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`). This setting name indicates it targets animated *thumbnails*, but here it influences whether the resized uploaded image preserves animation (via `*_instructions_animated` in `OptimizedImage.optimize`). That’s a legitimate, diff-grounded behavior/semantics concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it is incorrect vs. an intentional policy choice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No specs are added or updated in this diff — nothing covers the new `downsize` dimensions-string signature, the controller downsizing loop (success, non-convergence, convert failure), or the changed client-side limit; existing `OptimizedImage` specs calling `downsize(from, to, w, h)` would have exposed the duplicate-definition breakage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new behavior and API changes without any accompanying test changes visible here. Specifically: (1) `UploadsController#create_upload` now performs a retry loop calling `OptimizedImage.downsize` until the tempfile is under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, which has multiple branches/edge cases (non-convergence after 5 attempts, failures inside `downsize`, behavior for non-images). (2) `OptimizedImage` changes `resize`/`downsize` to pass a dimensions string and removes the `dimensions` helper, plus it now contains two `downsize` definitions (the latter overrides the former), so tests would be valuable to lock the intended signature and catch accidental breakage. (3) client-side max size is hardcoded to 10MB in two places, changing behavior that would ideally be covered. The finding is thus a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a generic “add tests.”
